Here it may be Enquired what is meant by Gods Hearing Prayer . & there are two thing s Implied in it .

_____________

1 . It is acepting the Pray the supplications of those that Pray to . he accepts them when they Come to him their address to him is well taken as that which G. is Pleased with . he approves of their Coming to him & approves of their asking such mercies as they Request of him & approves of their manner of doing of it . he accepts of their Prayers as an offering to him he accepts the honour they do him in Prayer .

2. He acts agreable to his acceptance & that two ways [--] 1. He sometimes manifests his acceptance of their Prayers by special discoveries that he makes of his mercy & sufficiency in Prayer. . G. is sometimes Pleased so to manifest his acceptance of his Peoples Prayers he Gives them special Communion with hims. in Prayer & while they are Calling upon he Comes as it were Comes to them & discovers hims to them & Gives them sweet views of his Glo . Grace & suf Mercy & sufficiency & also of his sovereignty . & Enables them sweetly with Great Quietness to Rest in him as in & Leave thems. & their Prayers with him submitting to his will & trusting in his Grace & faithfulness . such a manifesta. G. seems to have made of hims. to Hannah in Prayers[-] that so Quieted & Composed her mind & took [^001-note3] away her saddness we Read how Earnest she was & that in the first Chap. of the 1 of sam. how Earnest she was & how Exercised in her mind & that she was a woman of a sorrowf. sp but she Came & Poured out her soul before G. & spoke of out of the abund. of her Complaint & Grief & then we heard that she went away & did Eat & her Countenance was no more sad . v. 18 .. which seems to have been from some Refreshing discov. G. had made of hims.. to her to Enable her w Quickly to submit to his will & trust in his mercy whereby G. manifested his aceptance of her.

Jer. 31. 3 [-] ------ yea I have Loved thee with an Everlasting Love ------- There is a Prophecy in the foregoing Chapter of of the Restoration of Israel from their Captivity & dispersion which is Continued here in this Chapter . & herein this Context two things are set forth viz . 1 Gods former Kindness & Love to the Israel in days of old as in the first Clause of this v. the L. hath appeared of old unto me God has a special Respect to [--] his Love manifested to them in first Callling separating them from other People & Calling them to be his People therefore as in the Last Clause of this verse with Loving Kindness have I drawn thee th i. e. I manifested My Love to thee in bringing of thee home to my self to be my People at first.

_______________

& G. has Respect Particularly to his Great mercy shows the People in bringing of them out of Egypt & Carrying them through the wilderness to Canaan. as appears by the Preceeding verse Theref Thus. saith ---------------------------------------------

____________

2. Here is set forth Gods future Loving Kindness [-]. to Israel in the mercy that he will sho would show them in Times to Come as in the verses show them in Times to Come as in the verses following the Text again I will build thee & thou ----------------------------------------- --------------------- & so throughout the Chap. & 3. The Reason of Both is Given the words [^009-note1] of the Text yea I have Loved thee with an Everlasting Love. or with an Eternal Love with a Love that is without beginning & without End.. This is the foundation of Gods former Kindness to them this was the Reason why G. drov had driven them to him to be his People because he Loved them before they were drawn they their following G. Cleaving to G. & Choosing him to be their God & worshiping him was not the Cause [--] that G. Loved them but G. Loved them before & that was the Cause of their Cleaving to him & Choosing him. he Loved them & drew them to him so drew them to him to be his People & [-] to acknowledge him for their & [n-] serve him as their God. otherwise If G. had not Loved them first they never would have followed him nor served him. for in thems. they werent very much Inclined to the worship of other Gods & to depart from the True G. so in Egypt they [---] served other Gods as Josh. 24. 14. Put away your Gods which your Fathers served on the other side of the flood & and in Egypt. & Ezek. 20. 5. 6. 7. 8. --------------------------------

A Principle design of the apostle in their Epistle is to show the Excellency of the Gospel or of the new Dispen Sation Inspired by X alone the Law of the old Legal dispensa. by Moses and the Argument that he begins with is the Superiour Excellency & Glory of the Person through whose bonds it Comes was delivered his being so much more Excellence than those by whom he Spoke under the old Testament and Particularly his being more Excelleny than the Prophets & more Excellent than the Angels it being Chiefly by the ministration of Prophets & angels that [--] God Give Revelations under the old Testament & in the First Place he mentions the Prophets and Compares X with them in the Two first verses of the Epistle Chap. & of the Epistle . God who Finding times. & nextly Proceeds to Any one X with the Angels because of old God Reveald his mind by their ministration as in the 2d verse of the next Chapter For if the word spoken by angels was Stedfast & hearken & to Show the Supervisor Excellency of the old dispensation Introduced by X to the old Testam. which was by the ministration of angels The apostle thought this First Chap Excepting tw the two First verses P Run on while Spoke of the Prophets . Runs & Comparison be tween X and the angels In the third verse mentions his Excellency as he is in himself [^012-note1] & his Excellency in his works & the Honour which G. had Put upon him his Excellency in hims. in that he is the & in his works in upholding all things & our Sins & the Favour that G. had Put upon him in his Exaltation in his being Set down on the Right hand of the majesty on high In this his Exaltation G. had For Greater Favour upon him then Even he he did upon the angels for he was up alone the angels & made the of the angels. & therefore it follows in the 4. v. Being made so much better than the Angels the as he hath by Intent. \ e hi G. on thus Putting Greater Honour upon him then he Ever did upon the angels did us . Gave him no more than his this Honour of being Set above the angels was what be be defined & makes & was no more then to the Superiour Excellency of the name that Properly belonged to him by Inheritance & there in our Text the apostle the 5. v. which in the v. of the Text the apostle tells what that name is shows how X had by Inheritance obtaind a more Excellent nam than the angels. & therefor in the Text we may observe true Unity.

### 389. Rom. 3:11-12

### 389.Rom. 3'11-12(4_36) edited

Jonathan Edwards

_______________________________________April 1736.. Rom 3. 11-12. There is none that understandeth there is none that seeketh after G. They are all Gone out of the way they are together become unprofitable there is none that doth Good no not one

_______________

The apostle subject The drift of the apostle in all the former Part of this Epistle is to Establish the doc . of Justification By faith in Jesus X alone alone & to Prove that no man Can be Justified by .his own works and to this End he from the beginning of the Epistle to this place he Insists wholly on it to show that all that world are under sin & so st for that Reason Cant be Justified by their works or by any thing but faith in a saviour. in the first Chapt . he showed that the Gentile Θ how the Gentiles were under sin in the second Chap he shows how the Jews are under sin in this Third Chap in the beginning of this Chap he answ. he answers an objection & in the 9th sums up the matter & following verses he sums up the matter & then Proves what then are we any better than they --------------------------- ---------------- & then follow the Proves what he had Insisted on out of the O.T. as it is written there is none Righ.---------------------------------

----------------------------------------------------

-----------------------

The Passages here Quoted out of the Old Testam. are to Prove three things 1 That mankind are universally sinfull or that all of them are Corrupt. this is Chiefly aimed at in the 10. [^016-note1] 11. 12. v. -----------------------------------------

--------------------------

2 That all are not only Corrupt but that all are Every one is totally Corrupt in Every part This is aimed at in the Quotations in the 13. 14. 15. v where the several parts of the body are mentiond the throat the tongue the -------------- the tongue --- the Lips the mouth --- ------ & the feet ------ 3. that Everyone is not only Corrupt in Every Part but that in an Exceeding degree in the 16. 17. so as to have no Goodness & only badness and that to the most dreadfull degree in the l6 & this is what is aimed at in the 16. 17. 18. v. ---------

---------------------------------------------------------

----------------------------

In the Text there are five things Predicated of natural men . .. 1. That they dont understand i. e they neither Know G. nor to Know how how to seek or serve him. natural men many of them are taught Concerning G. & his ways but they are without understanding they dont Know neither Know nor Can they Learn.

____________________________________

2. that they dont seek after G . many seem of them seem to seek after G. they attend on the ap of Ex ordinances of Religion . yea & may be some of them have their minds very much Engaged in it but Yet they dont seek after God they they may Pray to G. & meditate [^016-note2] on him Earnestly & beg mercy of him. but yet they dont seek after G. it is only they seek thems. & not G.

__________________________

3 . That they are all Gone out of the way. natural man may to outward appearance be in the way of their duty they may be very Conscientious & may be & none that see see them may be able to say Charge say but that they Go in the way they should do . but yet in Reality they are not in the Right way but are out of the way they Even in ther those very duties of Relig. that seem Right to outward appearance are Going on in wrong ways.

________________________

4. They are to together become unprofitable this is th all natural men are unprofitable . the they are unprofitable servants tho tha some of them may seem to be Religious yet they dont serve G. bu but in all that they do they serve other masters yea they serve Gods Enemies.

_______________________________________

5. There is none that doth Good no not one many natural man seem to do many things that are Good they attend on the matter of their duty strictly may do very much in Religion some natural men do a Great deal that in is beneficial to their world to the Benefit of their fellow Creatures some natural men may be men of Great Good to the Publick but yet there is [^016-note3] none of them. that doth Good. no not so much as one doc. All that natural men do is wrong.

### 393. Jas. 2:18

### 393.Jas. 2'18 (5_36) edited

Jonathan Edwards

May 1736 James 2 18 yet a man may say thou hast faith & I have works: shew me thy Faith without thy works, & I will shew thee my Faith by my works There seemed to be some mistaken Principles & Ill Practices Prevailing amongst those that this Apostle Immediately directed his Epistle to arising from their misunderstanding & misImproving of the doc the apostle Paul had Insisted on of Justification by faith only which is the oc There was some of them Looking on faith as all and Good works as nothing did hence allow thems. in several Ill Practices Particularly their seemd to be Prevailing amongst ‘em a sp of Pride and an affecting ofly Greatness which made em to shew a Great Respect & Re an Inordinate Respect to Rich and men & men that made Grave appearance by their gay clothing & the Like but in the mean time despise had Poor men in Contemp. Hence they neglected the Poor & they were Great Greatly degenerated in a sp. of Charity the did not visit the Fatherless & widows in their . & tho they might Give Poor People Good words yet they sent em away Empty or did but Little for them & another thing Ill thing that was Prevailing amongst ‘em was that they were there were many amongst them that were of an unbridled tongue & Parti- [^020-note1] cularly they [were] was a Great deal of Evil speaking & backbiting & also Railinbittle bitter Railing & Prevailing amongst them herein appeared the Prevailing of a sp. of Envy & strife among them & many Evil a Great deal of Confusion and many Evil works as the Consequence of it There was also much of the Prevailing of aly sp & a sensual spirit amongst them & also a Great deal of Injustice and oppression . as appears by the Last Chp The Case being thus with them was the Reason that the apostle does in this so much Insist on the necessity of Good works he warns the not to be Hearers of the word only deceiving thems. & thinking that that will be sufficient to save them but that they be doers of the word . & tells t as 23 of the Prceding Chap. & tells them that if a man Continues. in the way of Gods Commands not being with Perseverance not being a forgetfull hearer but doer of the word that men shall be blessed in his deed & that if any man seem to be Relig & bridles not his tongue he deceives his own H. his Relig. is vain . & tells them & that Pure Religion & und as in the End of the three Last verses of the foregoing Chap. . & in this Chap he tells them how it is necessary that they should be universally obed. they must not only obey some but all of the Com [^020-note2] mands of G. as 10 11 v & to Confirm the necessity of it he tells them that puts them in mind that that is what they are at last to be Judgd by viz. their obedience to Gods Commands. Jam. 2 12 . so speak ye & particular then the apostle Particularly Insists on the neces necessity of works of Charity . & then the apostle Comes to that which had been the occasion of their flattering thems in Evil Practices viz their misunderstanding of & misapplying the doc . of Justification by faith & in the v. Preceding the Text tells them that faith if it hath not works is dead being alone & then Come in the words of the Text yea a man may say. In those words there is a Comparison made between two Kinds fo thin diffe rents Kinds of manifestations or Evidences of our Good Estate or Evidences of our having a saving Faith in Jesus X. of which I w would observe . . what is the thing to be manifested viz our having a saving Faith in J. X . it is faith that is the thing to be shewn for it is said shew my thy faith & I will shew thee my faith. & the faith that is spoken of w is that which is supposed to be saving . when it is said a may man may say thou hast Faith . the meaning of it is thou be [^020-note3] Pretendest that thou hast a a saving a Faith hast a faith that thouPretendest to be saving & when it is said shew my thy faith without thy works doubt it is Evident tis the same faith that is Pretended to be so shewed shewn that is spoken of in this next Clause & I will shew thee my faith by which doubtless is a saving faith for the apostles even account that faith that has works is not a dead faith but a Justifying Faith 2. we may obs. what manifestations of faith is spoken or to whom it is to be manifest & that is to our neighbour the apostle dont is not here speaking of the Evidence th of faith to out own Consciences bufo but of a manifestation of or Evidence of our Good Estate one to another. . shew me thy faith & I will shew thee my faith 3. we may obs. what are those Two Kinds of mani festations of a saving faith that are here Compared and they are a manifestation of it by words & a manifestation of it by deeds works. those two are spoken of in the first verse Clause a man may say thou hast faith & I have works the meanig is not thou has Indeed faith & nothing Else & I have works & no faith as is Evident by what follows . but thou sayst thou hast Faith & that is n the Princi [^020-note4] pel manifestation of your faith that you have but I have works . they are Two way of shewing our neighb. our faith that are spoken of . one is a shewing our faith without our works . t i. e a shewing of it by words there is no & the other is a shewing of it by works . there is but these two ways of shewing what is to our neighb. what is in our Hearts viz. by either by words or by deeds deeds & thereof when the apostle says shew my thy faith b without thy works he means shew it by words & I will shew thee mine by deeds 4. we may obs. to which of these the apostle Gives the Preference. viz a shewing of it by works. for the apostle here Preferences the man than that he Is supposed to speak - for when the for when the apostle says a man may say say his meanig Plainly is a man may Reasonably say . thou hast faith & I have works . shew me thy faith without thy works or by words only & I will Plainly Giving the Preference to the Latter the design of the apostle in supposing a man so speaking is to shew the Insufficiency of the former way . & how vastly Preferable the Latter is. [^020-note5]

doc. a manifestation of Godliness in s ones Life and walk is a better Ground of others Chaity Concerning his Godliness than any account that he Gives about it in words. This does is the Plain design & sense of the words of the words of the Text and as we Take the ss. for our Rule we have the same Reason to Receive this for truth as an other doctrine plainly taught us therein. shewing our faith to our neigh bour by our works is if we dont Reject the Text as false is Certainly the best way of shewing of and a more credible way than any way of whatever of shewing of it in words . it is a better way of others charity. [Several lines of space] I. Prop. men may in their Life and work hold forth to oth that to others which may be matter of Just & Rational Conviction to them that they are Godly . this it is a [mistake] that some seem too much to Embrace that there is no such thing as a mans Giving others [^020-note6]

Rational Ground to conclude he is Godly by his walk & that it Cant be done without Particularly Enquiring & Examining into his Experiences. this is Evidently a mistake for if it were so there would be no such thing as is our shewing our neighb. our faith by our works and if so why Did the apostle mean when s he spoke of such a thing and also spake of & when he not only speaks of their being such a thing as shewing manifesting our faith by our works but speaks to our neighbour by our works but speaks of it as the best manifesta that our neighbour Can have . if when a man have Lived & walked never so well we from thence have no Rational Ground to think him Godly then tis because he hant shewed us his faith & by his Life and walk. all that he has done is no shewing of faith & then whom did the apostle mean d when to he talked of shewingfaith by our neighbour our faith by works. that which is not held forth to the Eye of Reason is not shewn . if there be not Rational Ground of Conviction there is no mani festation. . There theref doubtless is such a things as a Persons holding forth to our having Rational Conviction to Judge for the True by the what we see of the Fruitthere is mans Light may doubtless so shine before men [^020-note7] by others seeing their Good works that others may have Rational Ground to Glorify there Heavenly Father for working in a Good work in the G. as being their Heavenly Father & from the Evidence of the Good work that he has seen he has wrought in them . no man Gives by any thing that we Can see in his Life & walk Let it be ne ver so Excellent Giv Can Give us such Evid of his Godliness t as that we Can Know that he is Godly but he may hold forth that which may be Rational Conviction & Ground for us to Embrace them as such in our Charity without hestia hesitation Here I would speak something to an Enquiry & ss we Cant see holiness by any thing Enquiry in mans walk for holiness is not an External b thing but tis what is Inward & Invisible and Gods Holy ones are hidden ones & the new name is that which no man Knows but he that Receives it but yet there may be such appearances of it in a mans Life & as may satisfy our Charity but Here & theref here I would say something to this Enq Enq. viz what appearances of Holiness there may be in our neighbour in what is visible to us. . ans. 1 a man may not There may be a Great appearance in what is visible to us as a mans being not only negatively but Positively of our Holy [^020-note8] & Xtian walk & Conversation . we may not only be able to say that we see nothing him but h that he may be a Good man. we see nothing in his Life and Conversation that is Inconsistent with his being Godly or that Contradicts such a supposition. but we may see in his behaviour a Great many Positive appearances & manifestations the man may seem In many ways to hold forth say that there is Positive that there has the fear of G. & the Love of G. or a & a Graci ious Charity & Love to man in his Heart. There are many men that Commonly are Called hon moral men or honest men & Conscientious me that are so Called Chiefly from what is negative i. e we have no special transgressions or Iniq. to Charge him he has Kept Clean from Gross sin & from any thing special that has appeard to the Eye of the . so some are Called Conscientious men whereby he has men that might wound his Reputation or being a blot in his Character some are Calld Conscientious men and are Generally so Esteemed when that which is observd in them whence they are so Called Consists Chiefly in negatives he dare not tell a Lie he is Just in his dealing. he dare not defraud his neigh bour. he durst no violate the sabboth he spea avoids ill Language & the Like . but men are Capable m their [^020-note9] to hold forth tosome me men are often Calld moral men & Conscientious men . of whom we have nothing to Remarkeably to say of that which is Positive of their bringing u forth much Positive fruit to Gods Honour of their Laying out thems. to do Good & walking as if they had their minds bent to Promote the [Inter]est of Religion & the Good of men & the Like we are taught X has taught us that men will here after be Condemned for negatives. in the account we have of the day of Judgmt when those at the Left hand have sentences Pronounced against them there is no mention made of these & those any special Immoralities or Irreligion they had been Guilty but on that they that they had faild of Bringing forth Positive fruit. I was an stranger & ye But men are Capable in their walk to hold forth that which is much more they may appear to be Positively of a holy & Xtian Life as to what is visible they may be those that do set thems. to some G. their Life may appear to be a Life of the service of G. as to what is visible they may seem to follow Xs Example to fill up their Lives as men with doing of Good. they may appear to Labour to do Good to mens souls & also to do Good to their bodies they may not only appear . they may seem so [^020-note10] for as is visible to Come up in a Great measure to those Excellent Rules of Life that X has Given in the 5 of math 6 & 7 of math & Elsewhere & the that the apostles have often Given in their Epistles . a th man may not only be of a walk that is not chargeable with any notable Perverseness . but he may be of an amiable walk & Conversa. he may not only be appear free of dark spots & blemishes & deformi notable deformities but he may shine. his Light may shine before men . 2. In what is visible in his walk their may be a Great appearance of his being universal in his obedience to Gods Commands. . some men that make Profession of Godliness tho it may be their walk for the most Part seems to be Good yet there are some Particular things in th them that seems to be stum notable stumbling blocks Concerning them . & some men that are Called moral & Conscientious men yet if they be [narrow] ly observed there are some by Paths that they have there are Certain Created ways that they are wont to turn aside to it may be the man is very devout & & strict in Keeping the Sabbath & in Going to me attending ordinances & the duty of Prayer & other Relig. duties But it may be in is a notoriously negligent man [^020-note11] about Paying his debts . & if he be not negligent in both strict in Relig. duties & also strictly Just & honest in his dealings yet it may be he is very bad with Respect to one that does a Great deal at backbiting & Evil speaking one that seems much to all be of a Contentious Quarrelsome spirit he is often fomenting of strife & [derision] & & is hotspirited & full of very Envy Envious & willfull. or if he be strict in Relig . & Just in his dealings & also avoids Publick strife yet it may be he is done that [d ] a Great deal at backbiting & spe whispering & speaking Evil of others behind their backs . & if he avoids this also it may it be it may obsrvd of him that he is notoriouslyly & a very Close fisted towards the Poor & Pri of a Private & narrow sp. & if besides all these other things he is Go liberal to the Poor & seems to be Ge nerous & Publick sp. it may be at the same time he is to be noted for his Pride & ambitious sp. & if he [Carries] well in all these Re spects abroad it may be there is stumbling something very stumbling in his [Carrige] in his Family to his wife or to his Children or servants. . & or if he be Clear here there may be some other Crooked way that he has. I dont now say how far a man may seem to be Chargeable with these things & yet we have [^020-note12] Charity for him that he may be a Good man but only this I say that the more universally a man seems to be of a Xian walk the stronger is the Ground for Charity . & it may be so that in what is visible in a mans walk he may appear very universal in his obedience & his observance of Xtian Rules he may not only appear universal in negatives or in avoiding things forbidden but he may seem very universal in Positivefruits in f fruits that may appear sobe an appearance of there being in him Xian fruits of all Kinds towards God & towards man There may be a Great appearance of the fear & Love of G. in his walk . & he may seem to universal in walking in Coming up answering the Rules of the Gosp with Respect to Love to men Love to the saints & Love to Enemies. Rules of forgiveness meekness & forgiveness . Rules of mercifullness & Charity & Looking not only at our own things but also on the things of others he may be uni versal seem to be universal in attending Rules of doing of Good . Rules of bridling his tongue he may walk Like a Xtian in the House of G. & carry it amiably there & he may walk as Lik amiably in his family . & he may behave like a Xtian in his attendance in his out w ordinary secular Business . & may well as a Xtian towards all his neighbors both in [^020-note13] his dealings with them & in his Conversation with like them he may Carry it Xtianlike towards his Friends & towards his Enemies he may behave Xtianl as a Xtian under affection towards superiours Inferiours & Equals he be may behave Xtian Like under affliction & in Prosperity . tho he Can do none of these things Perfectly yet he Cl there may be in him a Great appearance of all those things & that in an Eminet degree. There are two sorts of persons spoken of in here in this context viz Hypocrites & sincere saints & they seem to be here spoken of Interchangeably Hy first Hypocrites are spoken of in the 14v------ ____________________________ & then the sincerely Godly are spoken of in the 15 . 16. 17 & the former part of the seventeenth v. which is the Text. ___________

Thine Eyes shall see the King in his B. & that is them that are spoken of in the verses Immediately Preceding that walkest Right. & speaketh upr.----- &c ----- They shall behold the Land that is very far off . which Insinuat this is they that are spoken of before in the 14.v. viz the sinners in Zion .

The L. shall bring a nation against thee from far from the End of the [^021-note2] Earth & 64 v. and the L. shall scatter thee among all People from the one End of the Earth Even unto the other . & this a being Carried & this is

But Gods dealings towards the saints should be quite Contrary to this the Contrary of this their Eyes should see the King in his Beauty this here is doubtless mentiond as a thing that is the opposite of being Carried away to a far Country & the opposition will appear in if we Consid that there is an other in speaking of the King here the Prophet alludes the King of that Reignd in Jerusalem that was of the Lineage of David so that the meaning seems to be this that while the wicked are Carried away Captive to a very far diff Country way off & are from their own & are Cast out to the very Ends of the Earth thou shalt that walkest Righteously shall dwell in Peaceably & Quietly in the Land of Israel. while they are Carried away & made under the King of Israel while they are Carried far away & made slaves under a foreign Prince thou shall dwell at [^021-note3] home in the Land of Israel under the Peaceably & Happy Government of thine own King they thou shalt see the King of Israel es of Israel the King that Reigns in Zion Jerusalem in his beauty Reigning & Governing his People in Great Glory & Prosperity thou shalt see this Prosperity & thou shalt Enjoy the blessings of his Reign thou shalt Rejoice with the Gladness of Gods nation & Glory with his Inheritance as the Queen of sheba said of solomons subjects 2. Chron. 9. 7. Happy are thy men and and Happy are these thy servants which stand Continually before thy thee. Colos. . 3. 16. Let the word of X Dwell in you Richly in all wisdom Teaching & Ad monishing one another in Psalms & Hymns & spiritual songs singing with Grace in your Hearts to the Lord.

________________________________________________________________________

In these words I would Observe 1. what is the duty that is here Commanded. singing Praises to G. here is the Use of Psalms & hymns & spiritual songs Prescribed & this Use of them ["this" over "the"] that is here directed to is not reading . meerly Reding them or meditating on them but to be sung . singing with Grace &c--- or to the Lord.

________________________________________________________________________

2 . The manner This is Required to be done Publickly for tis not singing alone men 2. 1. Tis a Publick singing of Gods Praises that is ["1" over "2"] here menti Commanded . tis not singing alone by our selves for our own ex Edification only But for one anothers Edification . Teaching and admonishing one another . this is one way wherein we are to be the means of Each others Instruction . and a means whereby one means whereby the word of G. of particularly that part of the word that Con sists in Psalms & hymns & sp. songs is to dwell in us Richly in all wisdom . singing of Psalms is a Great help to a sp. Understanding of the Psalms. and. the mind of the H. Gh. in the Psalms is often times Conveyed in the while the Psalm is a singing . & as it tends is a means of a spiritual understanding of that Excellent part of the word of G. so our Pro by Publick [^025-note1] singing is a means to help one another to a such a spiritual understanding & thus by Publick singing one is a means of teaching and adm one & and admonishing or Instructing one another . not but that Private singing or saying Gods Praises alone if Persons have Convenient opportunity will be very is very suitable & Profitable & what a sp. of divine faith & Love tends to dispose Persons to . This Priv singing by our selves seems to be Recommended in Eph. 5. 19.speaking to your selves in Psalms & hymns & hymns 18 . 19. v. and be not drunk with wine but be filled with the sp. speaking to your selves in Psalms & hymns --------------- singing & making melody in Your Heart to the L. when Persons are filld with the sp. in it oftentimes naturally dispposes Persons to singing of Praises even when they are alone .

Rom 5 10 For if when we were Enemies we were Reconciled to God by the death of his son. -----

______________________________

The apostle Hitherto from the beginning of the Epistle to the beginning of this Chap. had Insisted on the doc of Justifica. by Faith alone. & having Partaken Particularly spoken to that in the Preceding Chap. in this Chap he Goes on to Consider the benefits that are Consequent on Justification or in the beginning of the Cha first cause Theref being Justified by Faith we have Peace with G. through our L. J. X.------------ & there are Hence benefits that follow Justificati flow from Justification that are here Particularly spoken of viz peace with G. & hope of Glory . peace with G. is mentiond in the first verse Therefore being Justif ---------------------------- a in the following verses he speaks of hope of Glory as a benefit flowe accompanying Justification . By whom also we have access into this Grace wherein we stand & Rejoice in hope of the Glory of G. . & then the apostle

_________________________

I I would show wherein. There is a Conjunction of Excellencies thus in the Person of X that is very admirable & upon those accounts . 1. There is a Conjunction of such Ex divine Excellencies in him as as in our manner of Concieving are most diverse one from another.

________

2.There is a Conjunction of such Excellencies in X as are indeed diverse & in one manner of Conceiving & which he would have seemd to us not consisten [^031-note4] consistint one with another on the same subject.

3. of such exce diverse Excellencies are Exercised in him towards men that seemed most Inconsistent one with another towards the same object.

* a Lion and a Lamb. tho very diverse kinds of creatures, & they both of them have their peculiar Excellencies . but there are such Excellencies in it so as may be Represented by the Conjoind or meeting to gether in X as may be Represented by the Excellencies of both those meeting together in the same subject the Excellency of the that wherein a Lion Excells is his strength. the majesty of his appearance & in his strength the majesty of his voice so that other beasts Tremble at the appearance of the Lion the appearance of the Lion is such as tends to strike a dred of upon men & Beast & when the Lion Roars the Beast of the forest tremble & the Lion Excells in strength in which by which he is accounted as it were the King of Beasts. the Lamb has Excellencies of also its Peculiar Excellencies but they are of a very different nature that which the Lamb excells in is its meekness & patience besides the Excellent nature of the Creature as Good for an being meat for food & yielding that which is fit for our Clothing.

deut 32. 40 41. 42.. The End of this ImmediFor I Lift my hand to Heaven. and say I Live forever If I whet my Glittering sword and mine hand take hold on Judgemt. I will Render veng. to mine Enemies and I will Reward them that hate me I will make mine Arrows drunk with Blood and my sword shall devour flesh) and that with the Blood of the slain from the beginning of Revenges on the Enemy .

Those words are part of the Prophetical song of moses The more Immediate End of this song was to foretell to the Jews how Exceeding apt they would be in after ‘times to apostatize from G. & to forwarn them what Judgmts they must expect for so doing [-] moses had abundantly warned them before but that they might have those warnings but not forget those warnings but have them Con tinually in mind they moses puts them by Gods direction into the form of a song. & d that & God bids moses teach it to the Chil of Israel that they might Get it by heart & be often Rehearing of it. in the foregoing part of this song G. had been foreshowing the Child of Israel what back backsliding & Corruptions they would be Liable to & the what Kind of Judgmts he would Execute upon them & G. is showing for their warning is dealivering the Punish mt that shall Come upon wicked men in General in the words we may Observe First what [^032-note1] the Punishmt is that is declared & threatened

___________

we 1. Tis their due Punishmt I will Render vengeance to mine Enemies I will Reward them that hate me. i. e. I wont fail of bringing the full Punishmt upon them that they do deserve

___________________________

2. The very Terrible manner of their punishmt here variously set forth by several strong metaphors viz Gods Gods whetting his Glittering sword. This [----] the sword of divine veng. is here Repre sented as very terrible in that tis a Glitteirng [--] sword the appearance distant appearance of it may well strike terrour into the Hearts of Gods Enemies. . & the terribleness of the Punishmt is further set forth by the whetting of this sword. G. will as it were whet his sword to Prepare it to do the more terrible Execution. the terribleness of the Punishmt is further set forth by that that Gods arrows shall be drunk with. Blood with the blood of the slain & of the Captives [--] & that his sword shall as it were devour & be Glutted with their flesh.

_________________________

2 we secondly we may observe after what manner this Punishmt is declared & threatened. viz with an oath tis not only an absolute [---] the threatening is not only very Positive but G. swears that he will thus Punish wicked men I [-] Lift up my hand to Heaven & say I Lived [^032-note2] forever. God Lifting of up of the bread was the action Particularly used on succoring & G. speaking of hims. of in Represents hims & Li as Lifting up his hand to H when he succor in their most slemn oaths Gen 14. 22. and abraham said to the King of sodom I have Lift up my Hand unto the L. the most high G. the Possessour of Heaven & Earth That I will not take from a thread own to a shea Latchet. . & G. speaking of hims. after the manner of men Represents hims. as Lifting up his Hand to H when he swears. so the angel that is spoken of in the 10 Chap of Revela. that is supposed to X [-] be X when he swears he Lifts up his hand to H. Rev. 10. 5. 6. and the angel which I saw stand upon the sea & upon the Earth Lifted up his hand to Heaven & swear by him that Liveth forever & Ever who Created Heaven & Earth the things that therein are & the Earth & the things that there should be Time no Longer.

___________________________

G. in the Text swears by his own Life that he will thus Execute vengeance on ungodly men & say I Live forever . He that Can swear by no Greater swears by hims. as the apostle observes Heb. 6. 3. G. often in ss. swears by his own Life as numb. 4. 21. as truly as I Live saith the L. all the Earth shall be filled with the Glo. of the L. & so Isai. 49. 18. as I Live saith the [^032-note3] L. then shall surely Clothe thee with them all as with an ornament & e-- & so in many other places

____________________

Thirdly - we may observe the Time when G. will swears that [---] Condition of this oath If I whet my Glittering sw. & my hands take Hold take Hold in Judgmt if they Continue Inpenitent so that it Comes to that as Less . i. e. If I bent Prevented by a timely Repentence if wicked men Continue in their wickedness & it Comes to that that the Case Requires that vengeance be Executed then will I do my hands take hold in Judgmt & that I sit on the throne of strict Justice. then will I do thus.

_______________

[-] Fourthly & Lastly we may observe the Time when G. swears that he will do this. viz from the beginning of Revenges on the Enemy..i. e as soon as Ever the appointed time or day of veng. Comes & so then forward in this Expression two things seem to be Implied. 1 Those that their Punishmt shall be 1 when their Punishmt shall begin viz as soon as ever the appointed time or day of vengeance Comes . we often Read in ss. of a day of vengeance & the day of wrath. the G. [----] with wicked men so as soon as ever that day of Revenges on the Enemy Comes men fro at the very beginning of G. will bring the deserved Punishmt on wicked men we G. [--] the G. bears with wicked men for the Present yet he wont be [-] strict to Punish [^032-note4] them but theri Pu G. swears that their Punishmt shall Come at the very be as soon as Ever the appointed day of Revenges Comes men at the very beginning of it . 2. That it shall never End. from the beginning of Revenges. viz from time forward G. will deal with them.

with 2. Here are two Circumstances of his appearance mentioned . viz the seat which he sat upon & the Crown that he wore. 1. his seat was a white Cloud . a Cloud is often made use of in ss. as a symbol of the divine majesty. so G. was want to appear in a Pillar of Cloud to his People in the wilderness . it was a white or bright Cloud. such as used to be made use of as a toke to betoken the divine Presence which such was the Cloud that G. was want to appear in in the [^037-note1] mo holy of Holies above the mercy it was a bright Cloud & Called a the Cloud of Glory . such a Cloud was that that G. manifested in his Presence by an on the mountain where X was transfigured. math 17. 5. while he yet spake hehold a briight Cloud overshadowed them & behold a voice out of the Cloud which said this is my beloved son -------------- Thus the Prophet daniel when he X therefore appears in a C or upon a Cloud to has denote his divinity & divine majesty & dignity. so when the Prophet daniel had a vision of J. X as setting up his Kingd in the world he appears to him as Coming in the Clouds of Heaven dan 7. 13.14 I saw in the night visions & behold one Like the son of man Came with the Clouds of Heaven & Came to the antient of days & they brought him near before him and there was Given him dominion & Glory & a Kingd. that all People nations & Languages should serve him his domin. is an Everlast. d. which shall not Pass away & his Ki that which shall not be destroyed.

Isai. 53. 3. -- a man of sorrows & acquainted with Grief. some of this to the St. Ind. July 1753. This Chap. is the Plainest & fullest Prophecy of Xs sufferings that is in all the old Test . The Jews in Xs time used to expect [--] the messiah to Come in such outward Glory & splendour Prosperity but this Prophecy i the Prophecy of Xs sufferings in this Chap. is so plain that many of the Later Jews to evade the force of it have feign'd two messiahs one a suffering messiash of the seed of Joseph & another appearing in Great Prosperous messiah of the seed of David. we ask the old Testament sometimes speaks of messiah as in Great affliction & suffering & in other Places of in Great Glory not Considering that being sensible that these things have only a Respect to the different states of the same messiah the one a state of Humiliation & suffering & the other a state of Exalta. & Glory.

_________________________

But tis prophecied here in this very Chap. that the Jews should Reject the true messiah & should not believe that he was the X on this very account viz that he was in such a Low & afflicted state as in the two verses before the Text. who hath believed ------------------------------------------

____________________________________________________________

-------- & this is mentioned a brought in in the Text as a Reason why they would Reject him he is despised & Rejected of m. a m. of sorrows & acq. ------ & we hid as it were [^039-note1] our faces from him he was despised & we Esteem ed him not.

________

He is spoken not only spoken of in the Text as one that had met with affliction & that had met with very Great afflictions but that he was a sorrow but that he had was a man of sorrows

______________

There are some that at some - times are in Great Pros meet with Great affliction & at other times meet with Great Prosperity & so have often Changes from [--] once and again from one to another . but it was not so with X he had in his state of Humi. while he lived on here on the Earth but he was a m. of sorrows. sorrow what was he continually Endured. [-] It was [later xo] what constantly attended him & & so he is found in the latter Clause of the text to be acquainted with Grief he he was acquainted with it as persons are acquainted with those that they Constantly dwell with.

Luke 10. 17. 18. And the seventy returned again with Joy saying Lord even the devils are subject to us unto us through thy Name And he said unto them II beheld satan as Lightning fall from Heaven . In the Preceeding Part of the Chap. we have an Account of X sending forth the seventy discip. to as Labour into his Harvest to Preach the Kingd. of G. & to Confirm their word by miracles. he sends them forth as Labourers into his Harvest as tis expressed in the 2d v. in these verses we have an account of their Return to their master after they had been forth in the Message on which he sent & had been Labouring in the work that he had set them about. Concerning which we may Observe three things . 1. How they are affected on this their Return to X They Returned with Joy. it was a time of very Probably when they went forth they went with Heaviness & fear upon their Hearts in Consideration of what X had told em of the Greatness & difficulty of that work that he sent them upon & the Great Opposition they should meet with for X told em that he sent them forth as sheep in the midst of wolves. but now when they Return had finished the work that done the work that G. had sent them the X had sent them upon & Re come to meet their Lord again that had sent they came not with Heavy but Joyfull Hearts. we are not only the [^040-note1] the that the the Joy with which their hearts were affected appears both in its being expressly said that they return'd with Joy but theiir Joy appears in what they say to their Lord & the manner of their speaking . but this being to second thing Obsevabl Observe 2
